advances: Conditional attainment over all compatible bodies on a fixed base under a stated original-depth compactness hypothesis.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Normalize continuous normals to Euclidean length one. At a fixed sampled base, moving the mark and changing the bodies and scale changes the cap threshold by at most the mark displacement plus the uniform change in $\varepsilon f\Gamma$, independently of the base tilt. A slab of width $h$ in each fiber of the radius-$R$ ball has volume at most $h\omega_{d-1}R^{d-1}$. The symmetric differences control the remaining error, and closed pure-base caps select finitely many fixed subsets. The joint continuity of the profile and covariance therefore gives convergence of all cap masses uniformly in the normals for aligned convergent marks. Infima and then maxima are continuous, the latter by compactness and Hausdorff approximation of the sampled fibers. The slab bound and $f\le1$ give the stated upper comparison at every mark. A strict trial family with $\beta_0<b$ has buffered value below $b$ for small scale. A minimizing sequence then lies in the original sublevel after invariant normalization and has a limit attaining the unrestricted infimum.

The heaviest fiber has volume at least $1/|P|$. Its own centroid has ordinary depth at least $q_0$ by 6769574fc1bd9f8d with $m$ equal to its full volume, since every ambient cap containing the mark captures its own cap or entire fiber. Ordinary depth is $A_{\mathrm{sec}}$-Lipschitz in the continuous mark and zero on each own boundary: choose an own supporting unit $u$ and use the slope from 155691fc3768c06f to extend its plane to a support at the mark on the full hull. The resulting nonvertical cap captures zero $d$-volume. Comparing with the nearest own boundary and the markwise upper comparison gives the stated distances. The shifts have Euclidean distance at most $\varepsilon\sqrt{\lambda_+}$, so for small scale the old source balls supply proper sections with uniform area; the covariance bounds give the coarea floor also in $\Gamma$-unit normalization. Energy monotonicity and equality at the centered ball from d90ba05577427854 give the two source floors.

For the lower comparison take an ordinary deepest mark. Every nonvertical buffered cap there gains an own-ball strip of width at least $\varepsilon(E_{\min}v_0^{1/d})^{1/N}\sqrt{\lambda_-}$, with area at least $\omega_{d-1}(\sqrt{3}r_s/2)^{d-1}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Thus it gains at least $c_1\varepsilon$ with $c_1$ the product of these constants excluding $\varepsilon$. At any mark, the least closed pure-base cap through its base has reserve at least $V_p/2$ over ordinary depth. To see this, add two opposite unit continuous tilts through the mark to a large multiple of its base normal. On bases off the old plane both caps keep the original full or empty status, and on plane bases the two continuous captures sum to each fiber volume. The smaller cap therefore costs at most the old pure-base mass less half its plane mass, which includes $V_p$. The same argument for a zero base normal covers rank zero. For small $\varepsilon$ the reserve is at least $c_1\varepsilon$, proving the lower comparison over both cap types. At buffered deepest marks the same reserve and the markwise upper comparison give the $v_0/4$ gap. Take ordinary approximating families within the original compact sublevel for the upper bound on the infimum. For the lower bound, outside that sublevel $\beta_\varepsilon\ge\beta_0>b>\beta_*+c_1\varepsilon$ for sufficiently small scale.
statement:
Fix a complete base $P$ in the body-tied profile setting. Let $\beta_\varepsilon$ be the maximum buffered depth divided by total sampled mass, and let $\beta_0$ denote its ordinary unbuffered version. Put $\beta_*=\inf_K\beta_0(K)$ over all positive compatible families on $P$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Assume $\beta_*<b<\gamma_d/k(P)$, where $k(P)$ counts parity classes in the inherited affine lattice, and assume every family with $\beta_0\le b$ has an invariant representative in a single compact class of positive compatible families, with $M=1$, $V_z\ge v_0>0$, $K_z\subset R B_d$, a common positive inradius, and $\lambda_- I\le\Sigma\le\lambda_+ I$ for positive $\lambda_-,\lambda_+$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the infimum of $\beta_\varepsilon$ over all positive compatible families on $P$ is attained. With $\omega_j=|B_j|$ and $\omega_0=1$, put $A_{\mathrm{sec}}=|P|\omega_{d-1}R^{d-1}$ and $C=A_{\mathrm{sec}}\sqrt{\lambda_+}$. There is $c_1>0$ such that uniformly on the compact class
$$
\beta_0+c_1\varepsilon\le\beta_\varepsilon\le\beta_0+C\varepsilon,
\qquad
\beta_*+c_1\varepsilon\le\inf_K\beta_\varepsilon(K)\le\beta_*+C\varepsilon.
$$
In these representatives put $q_0=\gamma_d/|P|$ and $r_s=q_0/(2A_{\mathrm{sec}})$. Ordinary deepest marks have own-boundary distance at least $q_0/A_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and buffered deepest marks have distance at least $(q_0-C\varepsilon)/A_{\mathrm{sec}}$. For small $\varepsilon$ these marks have own balls of radius $r_s$, the nonvertical own buffered sections are proper with uniform positive coarea under Euclidean-unit or $\Gamma$-unit normalization, and their closed pure-base depth exceeds the raw maximum buffered mass by at least $v_0/4$. At each such mark the energy is at least $E_{\min}=\omega_d r_s^d$ and $f\ge (E_{\min}v_0^{1/d})^{1/N}$.
title: Attainment and uniform proper cuts on an original-depth compact sublevel
